newsitem.title: FRANCE: French 1996 budget deficit totals 295.4 bln Ffr.
newsitem.headline: French 1996 budget deficit totals 295.4 bln Ffr.

text.p: The 1996 French budget deficit will total 295.4 billion francs, close to the government's initial target of 287.8 billion, the ministry of finance said on Wednesday.
The figure is 28 billion francs lower than the 1995 deficit "despite a difficult macroeconomic context," the ministry said in a statement.
Earlier Finance Minister Jean Arthuis said France's total public deficits for 1996 were expected to be limited to 4.1 percent of gross domestic product.
The ministry said that budget spending had been "mastered perfectly" with the increase in spending held below the rise in inflation for the first time.
Spending rose 1.7 percent compared with an increase in prices of two percent.
This development marks, for the second straight year, a significant reduction compared with (a rise of) 2.1 percent in 1995 and 4.6 percent in 1994," it said.
Total net receipts were 13.4-billion francs ($2.4 billion) lower than initially targeted. This shortfall was partially offset by gains from non-fiscal sources and by a fall in total charges.

Overall for the year, "the results confirmed a lacklustre value added tax situation, in conjunction with weaker economic growth than predicted, but also a major rise in corporate taxes", the ministry said.
Given the shortfall in revenues, the government achieved its budget goals "through a particularly significant savings effort," the ministry said.
